log.source: CBS News live updates (CBS projections; AP tally not found)
log.notes: I couldn't find an AP tally. CBS shows two Senate calls (VA Warner D, GA Ossoff D), both holds, and no House calls. NBC's results page (as of 7:49 PM ET, https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/senate-results) lists Senate D 36 / R 31, which doesn't separate called seats from holdovers, so I didn't use it. It also lists House D 12 / R 10, which I couldn't interpret reliably, and one explicit House call, FL-28 Gimenez (R). I counted only that call for the House, and it's not a flip. No live election-night projection of final seat totals was found. The CBS Battleground Tracker figure of D 229 for the House is from Oct. 25, before the election, so I left it out.

I couldn't find AP's tally, so the House counts are NBC's. The Senate counts are the previous reading, because NBC's Senate page shows 45 D and 34 R, which seems to include holdover seats, and the 35-seat count wasn't separable. Named Senate calls on the CNBC and NBC pages: D won GA, NH and NC (NC flipped from R), and R won FL (Moody, per AP), which is fewer than the previous reading. The Senate pickups figure (D 1) is the NC flip. The House pickup (D 1) is NC-11, and the CNBC page didn't say whether FL-22 is a flip.

I could not find AP's tally, so these figures are NBC News's (House page: https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/house-results; Senate page: https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/senate-results). The House Democratic count is 89 in the NBC summary but 87 in its all-races table. The Senate figures for races on the ballot this year are my own subtraction of the seats not up this year from NBC's totals (D 45, R 35). I found no live projection of final seat totals: NBC's page shows none, and the Decision Desk HQ page was rate-limited (a search snippet showed D 239 R 196 at 6:00 PM ET, which I did not treat as a live projection).

Senate figures are NBC's totals of 45 D and 36 R minus its listed holdovers of 34 D and 31 R, so they are derived. NBC's race table listed only 5 called races (3 D, 2 R), which doesn't match that, so the Senate split is uncertain. The House pickup count is only the NJ-7 flip that NBC names, and its total may be higher. Yahoo's 9:20 PM tally was lower (House D 73, R 36). I found no live seat-total projection; the Decision Desk HQ and NewsNation reports of a House majority call for Democrats are a control call, not a seat estimate, and I did not verify them on the pages themselves.
